title: How many times is each word said up to ninety?
description: The game is played for the numbers one to ninety. Counting the multiples of three, five and fifteen gives the times idli, vada and idli-vada are said, and a check puts each count back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of multiples of a number up to ninety is ninety shared into groups of that number. Watch for students who forget that idli-vada is counted inside idli and vada.

source: Figure it Out box 1, Q2, p.108
video_script.why: The child counts the multiples of three, five and fifteen up to ninety by sharing ninety into equal groups.
video_script.substitution: Count the multiples of a number up to ninety by sharing ninety into groups of that number.
video_script.anchor: children playing the idli-vada game up to ninety, with a number strip
video_script.payoff_line: Idli is said thirty times, vada eighteen times, and idli-vada six times

final_answer.spoken: idli is said thirty times, vada eighteen times, and idli-vada six times

maths_rules: idli-vada is counted inside both the idli count and the vada count
video_script.design: One idea: the count of multiples up to ninety is ninety shared into groups of the number. Same method as the book example: skip counting to find multiples.

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the idli-vada game.
<bookmark mark='game'/>The game is played for the numbers one to ninety.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many times is idli said, vada said, and idli-vada said?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the strip from 1 to 90; the multiples of 3 are marked with jumps of 3

marks.way: the example from the book is pointed to

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>Idli is said at every multiple of three, so we count the jumps of three.
<bookmark mark='share'/>We ask how many jumps of three fit in ninety.

beats.on_screen: Given: the game is played for 1 to 90; idli at multiples of 3, vada at multiples of 5, idli-vada at multiples of 15

marks.given: the three rules are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the game goes up to ninety. Idli is for threes, vada is for fives, and idli-vada is for fifteens.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many times idli, vada and idli-vada are said

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many times each word is said, counting idli-vada in both idli and vada.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: idli, multiples of 3 up to 90: 90 shared into 3s is 30

marks.idli: ninety is cut into groups of 3 and thirty groups are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='idli'/>Step one, count the idli, because ninety shared into threes gives thirty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: vada, multiples of 5 up to 90: 90 shared into 5s is 18

marks.vada: ninety is cut into groups of 5 and eighteen groups are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='vada'/>Step two, count the vada, because ninety shared into fives gives eighteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: idli-vada, multiples of 15 up to 90: 90 shared into 15s is 6

marks.both: ninety is cut into groups of 15 and six groups are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step three, count the idli-vada, because ninety shared into fifteens gives six.

marks.six: 6 x 15 = 90 is written and all three get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the counts back. Thirty threes make ninety, and eighteen fives make ninety.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six fifteens make ninety too, so all three counts are right.

beats.on_screen: Answer: idli 30 times, vada 18 times, idli-vada 6 times
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Idli is said thirty times, vada eighteen times, and idli-vada six times.
